---
title: "SPEC-4.0.5-v001"
subtitle: "Full code review — findings and fixes"
---

## Scope

A full review of the TabMaster AI codebase as of v4.0.4 (commit `a5dba57`):
every source file (`App.tsx`, all components, all services), the build
configuration (`vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `tailwind.config.js`),
the extension manifest, and the HTML entry point. The production build
(`tsc && vite build`) was verified before and after the changes.

All issues below were fixed in v4.0.5. They are ordered by severity.

## Findings and fixes

### 1. AI Studio CDN importmap shipped inside the extension (high)

**Where:** `app.html`

**Problem:** the page kept a leftover `<script type="importmap">` from the
original AI Studio prototype, mapping `react`, `react-dom`, `lucide-react`,
`@google/genai` (and even `vite` itself) to `https://aistudiocdn.com/…`
CDN URLs — at versions that don't match the project's dependencies
(React 19 in the map vs. React 18 in `package.json`). Vite copies the tag
verbatim into `dist/app.html`, so it shipped inside the extension, where:

- the inline script violates the Manifest V3 content-security policy
  (`script-src 'self'`), logging a CSP error on every launch; and
- had it ever been honored, module resolution would have been hijacked to
  remote, version-mismatched copies of the app's core libraries.

A `<link>` to Google Fonts (Inter) was also present — an external network
dependency for a font family that `tailwind.config.js` never references, so
it was pure dead weight.

**Fix:** removed both. `dist/app.html` now contains only the bundled
script/stylesheet references (1.21 kB → 0.38 kB).

### 2. Concurrent window renames lost in storage (high)

**Where:** `services/storageService.ts` + call sites in `App.tsx`

**Problem:** custom window names are stored as a single
`customWindowNames` map, and `saveCustomWindowName()` performs a
read-modify-write of the whole map. Several features saved many names *in
parallel* with `Promise.all(...)`:

- "Auto Name" (AI rename of all/checked windows)
- batch rename ("name1, name2, …")
- undo / redo of name changes

Each parallel writer read the same old map, merged in only its own key, and
wrote the result — so the last write won and **all other renames were
silently dropped from storage**. The UI looked correct until the next
reload, when the lost names reverted to defaults.

**Fix:** all writes now go through a serialized write queue (each write
chains on the previous one), and a new bulk `saveCustomWindowNames(map)`
persists any number of names in a single read-modify-write. All
multi-rename call sites in `App.tsx` use the bulk call.

### 3. "Apply to Windows" / "Undo Reorg" abort on stale tab ids (medium)

**Where:** `App.tsx` (`handleApplyAiOrganization`, `handleUndoReorg`)

**Problem:** the AI grouping result (and the undo snapshot) hold tab ids
captured earlier. If any of those tabs were closed in the meantime — or if
the model returned an id that never existed — `chrome.tabs.move` throws and
the whole reorganization aborts midway, leaving windows half-moved.

**Fix:** both operations now intersect the stored tab ids with the
currently open tabs before moving, and skip empty groups.

### 4. Toast notifications dismissed too early (medium)

**Where:** `App.tsx` (`showNotification`)

**Problem:** every toast armed its own 3-second `setTimeout` that
unconditionally cleared the notification state. If a second toast appeared
within 3 seconds of the first, the *first* toast's timer hid the *second*
toast almost immediately.

**Fix:** the hide timer is kept in a ref and cleared before each new toast.

### 5. Gemini error handling could mask the real error (medium)

**Where:** `services/geminiService.ts`

**Problem:** both API wrappers ran `error.message.includes('API_KEY')` in
their `catch` blocks. A rejection without a `.message` string (Gemini SDK
errors are not always `Error` instances) threw a `TypeError` inside the
`catch`, replacing the real failure and breaking the "invalid key → show
the API-key dialog" flow.

**Fix:** the check is now `String(error?.message || '').includes(...)`.

### 6. Unescaped URL interpolated into preview HTML (low)

**Where:** `services/tabService.ts` (`injectBaseTag`),
`components/PreviewPanel.tsx`

**Problem:** the tab URL was interpolated into `<base href="...">` without
escaping, so a `"` in a URL could break out of the attribute. Impact was
limited (previews render in a sandboxed iframe with scripts disabled), but
it was still an injection point — and `PreviewPanel` duplicated the same
injection logic inline instead of using the shared helper.

**Fix:** `injectBaseTag` escapes quotes; `PreviewPanel` now calls the
shared helper.

### 7. Unbounded thumbnail cache (low)

**Where:** `services/tabService.ts`

**Problem:** card-view thumbnails were cached per tab id and never evicted
when tabs closed, so the cache (full HTML captures, often hundreds of KB
each) grew without bound over a long session.

**Fix:** the cache is capped at 300 entries with oldest-first eviction
(recapture refreshes an entry's position).

### 8. Smaller items (low)

- **Leaked object URLs** — CSV/Markdown export and the User Guide download
  never called `URL.revokeObjectURL()`. Fixed in `App.tsx` and
  `UserGuideModal.tsx`.
- **Keyboard navigation vs. text inputs** — the global key handler only
  ignored `<input>` elements; it now also ignores `<textarea>`, `<select>`,
  and `contentEditable` targets.
- **`tailwind.config.js` scanned a nonexistent file** — `content` listed
  `./index.html` (the entry point is `app.html`). Harmless today because
  the HTML holds no Tailwind classes, but fixed so future classes in the
  entry page aren't purged.
- **Empty `.env.example`** — now documents the optional `API_KEY` build-time
  fallback used by `vite.config.ts` / `geminiService.ts`.
- **`DEFAULT_CARD_METADATA` typing** — declared as the optional
  `StorageData['cardMetadata']` type, forcing a non-null assertion in
  `App.tsx`. Now typed `CardMetadataSetting[]` and the assertion is gone.

## Reviewed and left as-is

Noted for the record; none of these blocks correct operation:

- **`metadata.json`** is an AI Studio scaffold artifact. Kept: harmless,
  and it documents the app description.
- **`handleUndoReorg` name loss** for windows that no longer exist —
  restored tabs go to a new window whose generated id has no stored name.
  Acknowledged in a code comment as a deliberate simplification.
- **Double sorting in `TabListView`** — the parent passes pre-sorted rows
  in controlled mode and the table sorts again with the same comparator.
  Redundant but stable and cheap.
- **`background.js`** is a stub (install log only) — intentional.
- **`constants.ts` mock data** is only used by the web-demo fallback path.
- Bundle size (~489 kB pre-gzip) is dominated by `@google/genai` +
  `lucide-react`; fine for an unpacked extension, no code-splitting needed.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (`tsc` strict type-check + Vite production build) passes.
- `dist/app.html` verified free of CDN references; `dist/manifest.json`
  carries the bumped version.
- `quarto render` regenerates this book without errors.

## Version

`package.json` and `manifest.json` bumped **4.0.4 → 4.0.5** (bug-fix
release, no feature changes). Tagged `v4.0.5`.
